1.web: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
1.asv: Boast not thyself of to-morrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

2.web: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
2.asv: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.

3.web: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
3.asv: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool’s vexation is heavier than they both.

4.web: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
4.asv: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?

5.web: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
5.asv: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.

6.web: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
6.asv: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

7.web: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
7.asv: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

8.web: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
8.asv: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.

9.web: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
9.asv: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man’s friend that cometh of hearty counsel.

10.web: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster: better is a neighbor who is near than a distant brother.
10.asv: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.

11.web: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
11.asv: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.

12.web: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
12.asv: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; Butthe simple pass on, and suffer for it.

13.web: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
13.asv: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for a foreign woman.

14.web: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
14.asv: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.

15.web: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
15.asv: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:

16.web: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
16.asv: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.

17.web: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
17.asv: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

18.web: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
18.asv: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.

19.web: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
19.asv: As in water faceanswerethto face, So the heart of man to man.

20.web: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
20.asv: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.

21.web: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
21.asv: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man istriedby his praise.

22.web: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
22.asv: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

23.web: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds:
23.asv: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, And look well to thy herds:

24.web: for riches are not forever, nor does even the crown endure to all generations.
24.asv: For riches are not for ever; And doth the crown endure unto all generations?

25.web: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
25.asv: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.

26.web: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
26.asv: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;

27.web: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
27.asv: Andthere will begoats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.
